title: Great Swan Song performances? "On Golden Pond" (1981)

commenti.body: I adore Joan Crawford’s final film performance in Trog. She’s performing like she wants the academy award. Apparently she always wanted to play Marie Curie but was denied. She gives everything in this B film as Dr. Brockton. Pay no mind to Rotten Tomatoes. This campy cult classic is a fun end to Act III of Crawford.

A Most Wanted Man / Philip Seymour Hoffman

  
One of his greatest performances, brilliantly melancholic and vulnerable. It's a real shame this film is so often  
overlooked as I think it's a hidden gem and one of his best performances. A guaranteed  
hit with anybody who loves a geo-political thriller.

Boris Karloff in Targets. And whatever you think of the films themselves, Bela Lugosi gave it his all under Ed Wood’s direction, bringing the same commitment and gravitas that he did to the Universal horror films. His famous monologue in Bride of the Monster is actually quite touching in a way, as if he were venting about his own frustrated ambitions in the film industry.

Chadwick Boseman in Ma Rainey’s Black Bottom was incredible and he was robbed of a posthumous Oscar for it. The Academy messed up, and sacrificed Joaquin Phoenix to beat the bad news. 

Fred Gwynne in My Cousin Vinnie. Glorious, funny, sincere work by the big guy.

Albert Finney in Network. He did get a posthumous Oscar for this angry af performance. 

Ann Miller and n Mulholland Drive. Her old Hollywood smarm was perfect, and she does look like she could be Justin Theroux’ mom.

I didn't have to think about this - it's Jason Robards in *Magnolia*. It's a truly wonderful performance. His long rambling monologue in the middle of the film just floors me every time. Think about that text on the page, and then think about where Robards takes it. What an actor. To me, Robards is the heart of *Magnolia* \- faltering, slowing down, processing a life of suffering and regret. It's so *real*. Still strikes me as an injustice Robards' performance was not recognised at the big awards ceremonies, all the attention getting snatched away by an irritating alien-bothering troll.

Edit: Damn - I've just thought of another great example for this post. Gunn Wallgren in Bergman's *Fanny And Alexander.* OK so this is the only film of hers I've seen, but it must surely be a great ending to her career. As the family matriarch she's warm, wise, charismatic, vital and alive - a miracle considering she was dying of cancer at the time and, if the reports I've read are true, often in physical pain. I almost wish I hadn't learned that particular piece of movie trivia, as it's hard not to think about it when watching the film. The fact not a single hint of her real experience seeps into her wonderful performance (at least not in any superficial way) is amazing.
I love this about Crawford - no matter what she’s  in, she gives it her all.
John Wayne in The Shootist. He may have been a prick, but he created/perfected an archetype that this movie is an elegy for, just as much as it’s an elegy for Wayne, who would die three years later.
He’s one of my favorites actually lol, and I do love The Shootist, James Stewart being in it is touching as well.
